question: What strengths and weaknesses do reviewers report for the Moto G7 camera?
answer:
One reviewer described the Moto G7 camera as terrible, saying scenic views and focusing were poor and almost every photo was out of focus. [280e64bc862d_0]
That same reviewer said the camera was okay for selfies and portraits but would not recommend the phone for great quality photos. [280e64bc862d_0]
Another reviewer said the camera is not good and that the Moto G4 Plus has a better camera. [24eda2ef28c5_0]
One reviewer said the front and rear cameras are decent for a budget handset. [7783db11b24b_1]
A reviewer who said they do not use the camera reported hearing that the camera is very good. [38050f99d3ad_0]
One reviewer said you can take decent pictures when the moment arrives, but that installing the Google Camera APK made a noticeable difference and brought the experience to a solid B+. [56c803e5693e_3]

chunks.text: I've owned several Moto Smartphones BUT. I've owned several Moto Smartphones BUT, the camera on this G7 is terrible. If all you take is selfies and portraits it is ok, scenic views poor, focusing poor. almost every photo is out of focus. However I like Android 9 Pie, clean OS but still a little buggy. In general I like the G7, I have no other issues, just the camera is exceptionally poor. I would return it if I could and another Moto Phone with a better camera. I would not recommend this phone if you are looking for great quality photo's. Great phone otherwise.

A Google search showed me that Moto's are notorious for Bluetooth connection issues. So, if you use Bluetooth, you may want to look elsewhere. I haven't used the camera much, but the fingerprint sensor worked flawlessly (so far, only had it less than 2 months, yet having all these unresolved problems). BY THE WAY, if you buy a brand new phone and it has a factory defect, Moto will replace it with a refurbished phone., which run about $100 cheaper. Seems to me, if you want a G7, a refurbish is the way to go so you don't lose a $100 in value like I did when it starts to have mystery problems.
A step up with the Moto g7. Upgraded from moto g5 bigger screen faster process time.i like the tear drop camera design.
I'm not enough of a camera geek to compare cameras. Otherwise, the Moto G7 delivers a comparable user experience to the Samsung S10 for 1/3 - 1/2 the price.
Camera not so good. Moto g4 plus has better camera.. Camera is not good. Rest is fine.

Moto G7 is not worth the price.. The seller delivered as posted but the Moto G7 does not meet Motorola's usual high quality. The best points are Motorola's high quality screen actions and sound. The front and rear camera are decent for a budget handset. The speaker is decent and serviceable but don't expect a lot out of it. You're better off using headphones or a Bluetooth speaker for music or videos. The battery is okay and with normal everyday use and you should be able to make it through an 8 hour day on a full charge. The phone runs smoothly for every day use but I wouldn't recommend for heavy graphic intensive game. The Moto G7 is not built for gaming, but then, no budget handset really is. That said, you can get by running some titles at minimal settings. PUBG Mobile and Real Racing 3 run smoothly enough, so long as you turn the graphics down. The G7 is water repellent (not water resistant), and it lacks NFC.

Facts About the Moto G7. The only thing I dislike about this phone was that it was still programmed to hook up to the old H and H+ server at times and caused me to miss calls. The Facial recognition doesn't really work either. If may light up but the phone won't unlock with facial recognition. Other than that the phone is legit. Good features and good price at 200.00 dollars. I'm definitely getting the new G8 plus

A capable and worthy upgrade to the G6. As an instructor using a variety of apps in a given course I switch between multiple apps in rapid sequence, often also needing to capture photographic images as well. The G6 was, at times, a tad slow to switch apps or to open and close the camera. The G7 is faster at switching among apps including the camera. The rear mounted fingerprint sensor is perfectly positioned, a real gain over the G6 with its face mounted sensor. Battery life feels longer as well. A worthy successor to the G6, a highly recommended upgrade for those in the G6. For those who are not accustomed to the Moto line, these are really clean machines. Pure Android, pure Google. Chrome browser, not some manufacturers reworking of Chrome. Motorola Motos and the G line are perhaps the best kept secret in the smartphone world.
